title: From Bigfoot to Mothman: SIU's Wild New Cryptozoology Showcase
byline: WSIU Public Broadcasting | By Brian Sapp
excerpt: Discover the new "Spoooked" cryptozoology exhibition at SIU’s Sharp Museum, featuring Bigfoot, Mothman, and cryptid art from across the country.
content:
Published October 27, 2026 at 3:00 PM CDT

In Southern Illinois, images of the Big Muddy Monster appear almost everywhere. You can see them on the sides of buildings, the backs of cars, or even on a statue in Murphysboro.

Creatures like the Big Muddy Monster belong in a category called cryptids. Cryptozoology is the study and search for animals that have been claimed to exist, but have never been proven. Think of Bigfoot or Sasquatch, the Loch Ness Monster, Mothman, or even the Jersey Devil.

If you want to see some of these creatures for yourself, head to SIU’s Sharp Museum. There, they have an exhibition called "Spoooked" or "Spooofed," a celebration of cryptozoology. The exhibit runs until December 11.

T. Lance, curator of exhibits, provided a tour of this exhibit.

The exhibit runs until December 11 at the Sharp Museum. The museum is open Tuesday through Friday from noon to 4:00 p.m., and Saturday from 1:00 to 4:00 p.m.
